No test report or other demonstration that ±50° is achieved appears in the programme documents returned by the search, so the capability is specified but not yet evidenced and must therefore be demonstrated or re‑evidenced.

cost.refused_because: Which kind of supplier work this requirement implies is not yet decided: the documents state verification = test but do not say whether the supplier must only provide test evidence for an existing design, or must redesign hardware (rack/housing) to achieve the angle. Find-comparable-work requires that classification (e.g. "validation_only" vs "modify_hardware").

decisions_for_human.question: Has the customer accepted reuse of an existing supplier baseline part (part number) for K2, or must the supplier deliver a new/modified rack+housing sized to permit ±50°?
decisions_for_human.why_it_matters: If reuse is allowed the job is likely validation-only (test reports, calibration) and is much cheaper; if a hardware change is required it becomes a design and verification job with larger cost, lead time and possible safety‑case impact.

decisions_for_human.question: Are the test conditions and pass/fail criteria for CR-K2-0102 (the test that must demonstrate ±50°) defined and agreed, or must the supplier propose them?
decisions_for_human.why_it_matters: The supplier must reference the test report to the requirement identifier; missing test conditions cause scope ambiguity and risk of rework if test acceptance criteria are disputed.

decisions_for_human.question: Does the supplier have to demonstrate road wheel angle permissiveness by inspection of mechanical end stops (dimensional inspection) or by dynamic on-vehicle/bench test?
decisions_for_human.why_it_matters: The verification method (inspection vs dynamic test) changes test rig needs, duration and cost materially.
